newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates fall back, supply better.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates fall back, supply better.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates fell on Tuesday after supply rose thanks to improved liquidity, money market dealers said.
"The banks' accounts are replenished, so trade was pretty much balanced," said dealer Radmila Nizetic.
She referred to a repayment of 142 million kuna to banks by the central bank after it cut reserve requirement by two percentage points to 31.85 percent of kuna deposits.
Total reserve payment was 3.3 billion kuna, the bank said.
Fresh money market trade was put at 35.5 million kuna, mostly in call money deals at 8.0 percent -- one percentage point lower than on Monday.
The one-week rate fell back to 10 percent again after a slight rise.
Two-week loans were granted at 12 percent and one-month at 15 percent.
The banking sector balances totalled 544 million kuna on Monday, compared to 320 at the end of last week.
Only one bank had a shortfall of less than one million kuna which it squared through overnight money market borrowing. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
